questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** It depends on the boot. For Blundstones, he says most come pretreated, so you don't need to treat them out of the box, but the distressed rustic styles are an exception that he recommends conditioning. As for how often, his most recent word (2022) is that there's no fixed schedule: treat them when they look or feel dry.

**Out of the box (2019 Blundstone videos)**
- He reads Blundstone's FAQ, which says most Blundstones are pretreated and "we do not recommend treating them out of the box" [1].
- The exceptions are rustic brown, Crazy Horse and rustic black leathers. They don't carry the same pretreatment, so you "may treat these leathers but do not have to" [2].
- For his own rustic pair, he says he recommends conditioning "100%" if you want the boots to last, though it will darken them [3].
- In practice, his untreated rustic pair held up in a year-later water test. He describes them as running on "basically factory oils and waxes" [4].

**How often**
- **Most recent (2022):** He says he doesn't know and expects flak either way. He admits he probably does it too little, and does it "when I feel like they need it" [5]. His cues are leather that looks or feels dry, or no longer beading water, which means it needs more wax or oil. Dirty boots should be cleaned regularly, because dirt wears leather down faster [5].
- **Earlier (2019):** He was firmer then. He said you may have to wax them "every month maybe every week" if you're really hard on them, and less if you're not [6]. He also said that any leather you haven't conditioned in a few months should be conditioned [3].

**Order when you do treat them (2022):** clean, then condition, then wax. The wax is the weatherproofing layer [7].

He has only covered this for Blundstones and leather generally. He hasn't given a schedule for other boot types.

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, the first soak or wash is when they shrink and get tighter, mostly in the waist. He hasn't covered what happens with repeated washes after that first soak.

**His most recent advice (2025):** He calls the 501 STF unsanforized denim that shrinks in the bathtub, and says you should usually go two sizes up. [1]

**How much they tighten depends on how you wash them (2023):** In his Wrangler comparison, his STFs shrank a bit in the leg opening and rise, and the shrunk pair looked far better because he didn't use very hot water and didn't dry them. He says that if you put them in the dryer, they'd start out a lot smaller. He also says that if you wash them similarly, the difference is negligible and he doubts you'd notice it. He adds that with frequent wear he bets they'd stretch out to about the same size. [2][3] His advice there is not to toss STFs in the dryer or rinse them that hot. [3]

**What it felt like on his first pair (2019–2020):**
- After his first hot soak and air-dry, the waist got very tight and the length barely changed. [4]
- A week later the waist and thighs had stretched enough to wear a belt. [5]
- A year on, he said the fit was good for him because he'd bought a small waist, though the pair was tight enough at first that he could barely pull it on. [6]
- He also said he wished he'd gone longer in length. [6]

**Not covered:** He doesn't say whether later regular washes keep shrinking them, beyond the dryer and hot-water points above.

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** applying his rule, he'd point you to a **35 waist and 32 length** (two sizes up in the waist, two inches longer). He hasn't said how 502 sizing compares with 501 STF, so this treats your 33x30 as your normal size.

**His latest view (2025):** he says of the 501 STF that you should usually go two sizes up [1]. In 2023 he added that the jeans shrink, which is why you size up two, and that the waist isn't vanity sized [2]. He also advises against hot water and the dryer, because that shrinks them harder. Soaking them in the tub and air-drying gave him a nice fit [3].

**The full rule (2021):** Levi's recommends two sizes bigger in the waist and two inches longer than you'd normally wear. After going through several pairs, he says Levi's is correct and that's what you should do [4]. He admits he'd ignored this advice at first [4]. He mentions that a 36 may not exist for someone who normally wears a 34, so check that a 35 is actually available [4].

**How his view changed:**
- **2019:** he skipped Levi's advice and bought his usual waist, partly because jeans are usually too long on him. He expected the waist to stretch [5].
- **2020:** he said the tight waist ended up being a good fit for him. He added that he should have bought a 32 length and cuffed them anyway [6].
- **2021:** by this point he had switched to recommending the full two-up rule [4].

He's cuffed his jeans to deal with extra length, so a 32 can be cuffed if it's too long [6].

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
By 2021 he described cuffing as a stopgap, not a firm preference: he can't decide between no, half or full break, and cuffing is the only fix he's found short of settling on one fit.

**Newest view (2021)**
- He says he wants clothes to fit differently depending on his mood, so he's never sure about hem length. The only solution he can find, "besides settling on one specific fit, which I will soon when I actually go out and buy my perfect-fitting pair of jeans, is cuffing." [1]
- He also notes that cuffs make your legs look shorter. [2]
- By 2023 he mentions that a pair of jeans was hemmed recently so they fit him really well, which fits that move away from cuffing. [3]

**Earlier reasons (2019–2020)**
- **Length:** In 2019 he said it's all about length for him, and that if jeans look too long they just look bad. He cuffed his Levi's 501s partly for that reason. [4]
- **Style:** In 2020 he said he cuffed his 501s because he doesn't think his current style suits wider-legged pants left uncuffed. He also said he should have bought a 32 length. [5]
- **Over the boots:** In 2019 he said he used to always cuff his jeans, but now likes them over his boots more. [6]

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** He has generally put the 3335s ahead of the 1907s, but by September 2023 he hedged on that, saying the 3335s "still might be" his favorite Red Wings but "probably not." He was also selling them.

**Most recent (Sept 2023):** He says he is on record calling the 3335s his favorite Red Wings of all time. He then hedges: they "still might be but they probably not," and he lists the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers as having characteristics he really likes [4]. He still likes the 3335s for their stitch-down construction, lighter weight and nimbleness, but he says they're going out of the collection [5].

**Earlier in 2023 (Jan):** He calls the 3335s "my favorite Red Wings to date" [3].

**Oct 2022:** This was his strongest preference. He says the 3335s are his favorite boots he's ever had and that they beat the 1907s and the 875s [1]. His reason is that he's hiking and walking in the woods rather than doing heritage work, and he calls the 3335s a dramatically better all-around boot. He adds that the 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so if you need a tough boot the 3335s are probably not the ones to go for [2].

**His love for the 1907s:** In 2021 he recommended the 1907s as the Red Wing moc toe to get [7]. He also recommended them in a fall essentials video [6].

**Bottom line:** For his own hiking and walking, he preferred the 3335s as of 2022–early 2023. By late 2023 he was less sure, and he's moved the 3335s along.

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of his most recent video here (September 2023), he still rates Blundstones highly: he calls them "incredible" and says he's a big fan, but he's retiring his heavily worn 585s as part of culling his boot collection, not because he's soured on them.

**Latest view (Sept 2023)**
- He says the 585s, the subject of his first-ever video, have held up through constant wear, and remain "probably my most water resistant boots" [1].
- He notes some people really don't like them, but says he's always loved them [1].
- Still, he says "it's time to retire those bunnies" [1].
- He groups Blundstones with other slip-ons as shoes he can flop on quickly for errands or rain, and says he's keeping a slip-on pair but could easily put it on the sell list [2].
- He's also letting go of his heavy-duty Blundstone Extreme work boots [3].

**How his view developed**
- 2019: he called them his favourite boots of his three or four pairs, recommending them if you keep them treated [4]. His main gripe was that the cemented soles can't officially be replaced [5].
- 2020: after a year he said they're still great, but he'd choose a smoother leather over the rustic nubuck, and that they're decent but not exceptional as work boots [6][7].
- 2022: he said he thinks they're worth the hype, though they're not as repairable as Goodyear-welted boots like Red Wings or Wolverines [8].

So overall he's still a fan as of late 2023. He hasn't said anything more recent in the videos available here.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He thinks Solovair beats the Made in England Dr. Martens, and his view hasn't changed since 2022. In 2023 he still liked his Solovairs despite their problems.

**Overall verdict**
- In his 2023 head-to-head, he says "the answer is Sol of a is better and Doc Martins is worse" [1].
- He says the Solovairs are about $40 cheaper, so you get "a better boot that costs less" with no artificial Doc Martens markup [2].
- In a separate video he says the England pair probably isn't worth the extra $90 unless you're a huge Doc Martens fan [3][4].

**Construction and materials**
- **Midsole:** England Docs have felted midsoles, but Solovair's are thicker, heavier and more robust. That means more padding and warmth, and they take longer to crush [5].
- **Comfort:** he notes Solovairs have a shank, which Docs lack, so they're more comfortable over long periods. Docs are easier to break in, though [6].
- **Repair:** Solovair soles are available on their website, and they will do the repair themselves. Doc soles are very hard to get, which is why he says Solovairs have a much longer lifespan [7].
- **Leather:** in 2022 he said the England leather is probably on par with Solovair's [8]. In 2023 he says Solovair often uses full grain, such as the waxed "greasy" leather on the 8-eye Derby [9]. It's not guaranteed on every model, so he says to check before buying.

**When he'd still pick the England Docs**
- He says if the yellow stitching matters to you, you have to get the Made in England Docs [10].
- He says big fans who want something like the old-style Docs have to go Made in England, "no question" [3].

**Solovair's downsides**
- His first pair had a back tab rip off and laces fray. He suspects the rough eyelets are the cause and says it's his "only gripe" with Solovair [11].
- Sizing was off: his Derbys came very big, and he suggests sizing down a half size [12].
- In September 2023 he said that despite those issues he really likes his Solovair monkey boots. He found them loose, probably from sizing wrong, and would only sell them to buy another pair of monkey boots [13][14].

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** He hasn't covered multi-day hikes in Blundstones. The closest thing is his own experience on day hikes, and it points to "possible, but not ideal."

**What he found on mountain hikes (2020):** He took his Blundstones up and down several mountains in Maine and says they "held up well" [1]. He also says they are "not good boots for mountaining" because they lack good ankle support [1]. Over four days with a pack on uneven ground, that ankle support is the biggest concern based on his comments.

**Comfort and break-in:** On a first walk in them he had no blisters [2]. Later, when he started running and walking the track in them, he got "big fat gross blisters like break-in blisters" for about two to three weeks [3]. By his experience, you'd want them well broken in before a long trip.

**Weather:** In 2023 he said his worn pair stayed "probably my most water resistant boots" [4]. He treats them as water resistant, not waterproof. He wouldn't stand in water for hours, though they were fine for crossing a stream or standing in mud [5][6]. His rule is that they only stay water resistant if you keep them treated [7].

**Overall:** He calls them decent but not exceptional for work [8]. He never recommends them as a hiking boot. He did keep a Hoka hiking boot for hiking comparisons in 2023, which suggests he sees them as separate tools [9]. He hasn't said how Blundstones cope with a heavy load or several days in a row.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** For your build, he'd point you to the **Muji tee**. His most recent word (Sept 2025) is that Uniqlo's $20 tee is probably the best you can get for the price, but anyone taller or wider should go Muji instead. He hasn't given a specific size for 5'11" and 225 lbs.

**Why Muji for you**
- He calls the Uniqlo tee probably the best t-shirt you can get for the price at $20, and the 'starter' tee. [1]
- He then says that if you're taller or wider in any way, you'd want Muji. [2]
- It costs a bit more, but he says it is significantly longer and a good deal wider. [2]
- In an earlier video (June 2025) he said Muji is about $10 more than Uniqlo and that the extra feels justified, with a slightly thicker, tighter collar and a nicer feel. [3] The price gap differs between the two videos.

**Other value picks**
- **Front General Store** is a $40, 100% made-in-Japan tee. He likes its proportions and feel, and it was his pick among the budget tees. [4][5]
- **House of Blanks** is a $35 combed ringspun tee cut and sewn in Canada, with no torque (twisting) at all. He calls it an outstanding value. [6]
- He says Front General Store suits you if you want character, and House of Blanks if you want perfectly smooth. [5]

**Size**
- He hasn't given a size for your height and weight. His sizing advice is about each brand's cut. Muji already runs longer and wider than Uniqlo, which is why he steers bigger guys there. [2]

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
You're not alone, and he says as much. By 2025 he no longer names one best t-shirt, saying it "just has to line up with your preferences to be the best t-shirt" [1]. In 2024 he did crown an overall winner, Asket, as "the silkiest densest most interesting shirt" [2]. His latest advice is to pick by the feel you want, and he does give personal favourites.

**If you want 3 to buy, his picks point to:**
- **J. Press x American Trench** is his pick among the all-arounders, which he'd recommend to "absolutely anybody". He chose it over 3Sixteen for its rougher hand feel and more structure [3].
- **Front General Store or House of Blanks** is his best-value pick. He says that if you like character and feel, go Front General Store, and if you like perfectly smooth with no torque, go House of Blanks. Of the two, "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store" [4]. House of Blanks is $35 with "Absolutely zero torquing on this shirt whatsoever" [5].
- **Uniqlo** is the cheap starter. He says at $20 it is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [6]. He calls it "your starter t-shirt", and says to get Muji instead if you're taller or wider [7].

**If you want to spend more:**
- He gives his Supremes category to Merz b. Schwanen's 2M15, which "eekes out just a little bit" over Lady White [8].
- In his Japan category he picked Wonder Looper over Samurai for its "much more universal fit" [9].

He hasn't said one shirt beats all the others. The best I can do for you is that his answer depends on whether you prefer rough and structured or smooth and silky.

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
He prefers the 1907 over the 875 and tells anyone looking at a moc toe Red Wing to get it. The main differences are the 1907's storm welt and a few extras for about $10 more. He later named the Red Wing 3335 as his favorite boot over both.

**Welt construction**
- He says the 875 is Goodyear welted, which he calls very durable and pretty water resistant [1].
- The 1907 has a storm (Norwegian-like) welt, which he calls "invaluable" [2].
- He relays the popular view that Red Wing's version is just another strip of leather stitched onto the welt. He says he's not quite sure that's how it works [3].

**Price and extras**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875 [4].
- For that you get a removable leather footbed, which he says is typically $40 separately [5].
- You also get leather laces, typically $15 [5].
- He says that makes the 1907 a better deal.

**Water resistance**
- In his standing-in-water test, the 1907's right boot leaked almost immediately through the stitching while the left stayed dry [6].
- He still has no doubt they'd hold up fine in rain, grass or mud [6].
- In a later video he says leather welted boots aren't really strong on water resistance, and that he'd rather wear injection-molded Blundstones in wet weather. He still highly recommends the 1907 [7].

**What they share**
- Both have crepe soles. He says he doesn't really like them, and that they break down faster than the 3335's Vibram sole [8][9].
- He calls both more beefily constructed, which suits you if you need a tough boot [10].

**Where this leaves things**
He has said he hasn't directly compared sizing or break-in between the two beyond what's above, so there's nothing more from him on that.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** Uniqlo is his pick for the best-value budget tee, and Front General Store is the one he prefers if you'll pay about $40 for more character. In his most recent video (September 2025), he calls the $20 Uniqlo tee "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. In that same video's winner circle for value, he says "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store" [2]. He doesn't rank Pro Club or Hanes above either of them.

**Uniqlo.** He calls it a "starter t-shirt" and says it's open-end and rather rough [3]. A June 2025 video says that at $15 it is very good, with a bound neck collar that doesn't wiggle, and that you "could end the video here" [4]. In 2024 he called the heavyweight crew "the best bargain t-shirt" [5] and gave it his superlative for best value heavyweight or all-around tee [6]. He measured shrinkage of 2.3% in width and 2% in length on one of the Uniqlo tees [7].

**Front General Store.** He describes a $40, 100% Japan-made shirt with "Great proportions, great feel" [8]. In 2024 he called it "one of the best shirts that you could possibly get," though a little rougher because of open-end yarn that has been sanded for softness. It is pre-washed and had a softness score of 6/10 [9]. It costs about double Uniqlo's price, so it's the pick if you want character and a Japanese-made shirt rather than the lowest price.

**Pro Club.** In 2024 he liked it and understood why people are passionate about it, but it was the roughest shirt on that list [10]. He gave it a softness score of 4/10 and measured shrinkage of 2.78% in width and 6.86% in length [10]. He didn't name it as a value pick.

**Hanes.** He called it "your classic $10 great shirt" [11]. It was much softer than Pro Club, at 7/10, with shrinkage of 1.45% in width and 6.73% in length [11]. Separately, in June 2025 he said ultra-cheap shirts from huge brands like Hanes and Gildan cost very little but all five he had showed a defect [12]. That is his main caution about the very cheapest shirts.

questions.question: Would you recommend this [Barbour Bedale] or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
**He leans toward the Bedale for rain plus wind plus spring use, but he never compared the two head to head for that job.** The Flint and Tinder is the easier, cheaper all-rounder, while the Bedale has far more rain-specific features.

**Barbour Bedale**
- In his 2025 ranking it was the top viewer pick. He says you can toss it on any time of year and be comfortable, with room to layer under it [1].
- He also says it's "not a designated rain jacket," since the fabric is lightweight [2].
- It has storm cuffs, which he calls helpful in inclement weather [3], and a throat latch he loves [4].
- In his 2021 guide he praised its storm flap behind the zipper, which stops water running through the zipper [5]. He also highly suggests buying the snap-on hood [6].
- In his shower test, a freshly waxed Bedale didn't leak at all [7].
- The catch is upkeep. Once the wax wears down over a few seasons, he says it won't be that waterproof or water resistant and water will come right in [8].

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker**
- In 2025 he says it's for everyone, and not crazy lightweight but a lighter weight, so it's comfortable [9]. He also likes that it's lined and costs $300 for a US-made, lined waxed jacket [10]. That segment was sponsored by Huckberry, though he says he'd praised the jacket many times before the sponsorship [11].
- In 2023 he said it was for a specific man that is not me, while adding that it's not a bad jacket [12]. He described it as fully lined in polyester [13].
- He hasn't said anything in the videos available here about how it handles rain or wind. He doesn't mention a storm flap, throat latch or storm cuffs for it.

**Bottom line:** if rain and wind protection matter most, his comments favor the Bedale, with the hood and a re-wax when needed. If you mainly want a comfortable, lined, easy spring jacket for less, he'd point you to the Flint and Tinder.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
He isn't saying lined Huckberry jackets don't exist. The con in that video is about the unlined version he tested, and he has praised the lined one elsewhere. His 2025 view also softened on lining in general.

**What the con refers to (Sept 2023):** He calls the jacket in that video "the cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket on this list" [1]. He then states the con as: "the one con that Rogue territory and huckberry have for me is that they are not lined" [2]. It's a personal preference. He says he always likes a lining on wax jackets so the wax isn't touching your clothes or arms [2]. He doesn't mention the lined versions in that video.

**He knows about the lined versions:**
- In 2022 he reviewed the flannel-lined jacket and noted that "huckberry does offer one without a lining" [3].
- In April 2023 he corrected himself to say there is a wool-lined version, but it "comes in dramatically more limited quantity" [4].
- In 2025 he calls the lined Flint and Tinder trucker comfortable because "You don't get wax on your skin" [5]. He says they also make a wool-lined one that he's "yet to get" [6].

**His lining preference has loosened (May 2025):** About the unlined Rogue Territory jacket, he says that while he usually wants a liner on wax jackets, "in my old age, as I've fallen old over the years, I kind of see why you wouldn't line something" [7]. So the lining con is less firm for him than in 2023, though he still presents the lined Huckberry as the comfortable option [5].

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't directly compared the fit of the Red Wing 3335s and the 875s in the videos available here, but he does describe the 3335's fit.

**3335 fit:** He went true to size and says they fit fine [1]. He notes a slim, tapered profile. With thin cotton socks in warm weather he felt no tightness, but with wool socks his toes feel squished and he can't wiggle them much [1].

**875 / moc toe fit:** He gives no sizing advice for the 875 specifically. About the Red Wing moc toe style in general, he says he thinks the toe box is a little large [2]. That is the opposite of the 3335's slim, tapered feel, though he doesn't draw that comparison himself. He also says the 875s and 1907s are more beefily constructed than the 3335s, but that is about build, not fit [3].

**Red Wing sizing in general:** He usually wears an 8 in boots, bought an 8 in Red Wings (the 1907s) and says they fit perfect. He advises buying leather boots snug but not squished [4].
